lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to World 20, Festival Island! This is the last world of Stage 2. Listen. Boom, boom, boom! What's that sound? I can hear drums. There's a festival on the island! Say it with me. There's a festival on the island! Great! There's means something is here. There's a big tree. There's a small boat. ワールド20 は おまつりの しま。ステージ2 の さいごの ワールドだよ。 Let's practice. Look at the beach. There's a red flag. There are many lanterns. I can hear the waves. I can hear the birds. Now, phonics. Picture. Culture. Mixture. Gesture. The t u r e at the end says chur. The E is quiet. Let's make a gesture. Wave your hand! Now, tell me. Close your eyes. What can you hear? I can hear the drums. Let's go and see the festival!

Would you like to come to the festival? Say it with me. Would you like to come to the festival? Nice! Would you like to is a polite way to invite someone. It's softer than Do you want to. Answer, Yes, I'd love to! Would you like to ～? は ていねいな さそいかた。 Let's practice. Would you like to play tag? Yes, I'd love to! Would you like to see the dance? Sure! Now, phonics. Treasure. Measure. Pleasure. The s u r e says zher. Treasure, not trea-chur. Nature has t u r e, so it says chur. Listen. Treasure, nature. Now, invite me! Would you like to come to my house?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Let's make invitation cards for our festival friends. An invitation tells three things. When? Where? What? Listen. Dear friends, please come to our festival on Saturday. It starts at five o'clock. We hope to see you there! Say it with me. Please come to our festival on Saturday. Wonderful! しょうたいじょうには「いつ・どこで・なにを」を かこう。 Let's practice. Please come to my party on Sunday. It starts at two o'clock. It's at the park. We hope to see you there! Now, phonics review. Picture, chur. Treasure, zher. Cure, yoor. Future, chur. Draw a picture of a lantern on your card! One more thing. Never write your home address on the internet. Paper cards for friends are fine. Now, read your invitation to me. When is it? What time does it start?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! In the fall, many countries have a harvest festival. Harvest means picking rice, fruit, and vegetables from the fields. At the festival, we say thank you for the food. Say it with me. We say thank you for the food. Wonderful! Farmers grow rice and vegetables. In Japan, too, there are fall festivals for the rice harvest. しゅうかくさいは たべものに ありがとうを いう おまつり。 Let's practice. We say thank you to the farmers. We say thank you for the rain and the sun. Now, phonics. Dear. Deer. They sound the same, but the spelling is different. Dear has e a r. Deer has e e r. A deer is an animal. Dear is for letters, like Dear Grandma. Appear. Engineer. Now, tell me. What food do you want to say thank you for?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Brr, imagine winter. In some cold countries, people have winter light festivals. Listen to the plan for this winter. There will be lights all over the town. Say it with me. There will be lights all over the town. Great! There will be means something will be there later. Use There is for now. Use There will be for the future. There will be は「これから ～が ある」と いう いいかた。 Let's practice. There will be a big tree in the square. There will be music. It will be cold, so wear a warm coat. Now, phonics. Bear. Wear. The e a r says air. Learn. Earth. The e a r says er. Near says eer. One spelling, three sounds! Now, tell me. What will there be at your winter festival?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we're visiting my aunt's house on the island. When guests come, hosts say, Come on in. Make yourself at home. Say it with me. Make yourself at home. Great! It means, relax and feel comfortable here, like in your own home. Make yourself at home. は「くつろいでね」と いう もてなしの ことば。 Guests can say, Thank you. What a lovely house! Let's practice. Come on in. Please take off your shoes here. Please sit down. Would you like a cushion? Guests say, Thank you so much. Hosts say, Please make yourself at home. Relax! Now, phonics. About. Again. Away. Alone. The first a is very weak. It sounds like uh. Uh-bout. Uh-gain. This weak sound is very common in English. Now, I'm your guest. Knock, knock! What do you say?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! It's snack time at my aunt's house. When we offer food or drinks, we say, Would you like some tea? Say it with me. Would you like some tea? Very nice! Answer, Yes, please. Or, No, thank you. Remember, Would you like to is for inviting. Would you like some is for offering things. Would you like some ～? は たべものや のみものを すすめる いいかた。 Let's practice. Would you like some cake? Yes, please. Would you like some juice? No, thank you. I'm full. Would you like some water? Yes, please. Would you like some more? No, thank you. Now, phonics. Banana. Sofa. Panda. Zebra. The last a is weak. Uh. Banan-uh. Sof-uh. Don't say banana-ah. Now, I'll be the host. Would you like some banana cake? What do you say?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! It's time to leave my aunt's house. When we leave a friend's house, we say thank you. Thank you for having me. Say it with me. Thank you for having me. Perfect! Having me means inviting me to your house. Then, add, I had a great time. The host says, Please come again! よその いえを でる ときは Thank you for having me. と いおう。 Let's practice. Thank you for the delicious cake. Thank you for showing me your garden. I had a great time. Thank you for the lovely lemon tea, too. Now, phonics. Lemon. Melon. Seven. Garden. The o and the e are weak here. Lem-un. Sev-un. A weak sound can be spelled with any vowel letter. Now, say goodbye to me. What do you say when you leave?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Yesterday, Grandpa Toma, my aunt's father, told us a story. When he was little, he was scared of drums. Now he plays the biggest drum at the festival! Let's talk about when we were little. When I was little, I was scared of drums. Say it with me. When I was little, I was scared of drums. Great! When I was little は「ちいさい ころ」。むかしの ことなので was を つかうよ。 Now I love them! Let's practice. When I was little, I couldn't ride a bike. When I was five, I couldn't swim. Everyone was scared of something. That's OK. We grow little by little. Now, phonics. Festival. Parade. Balloon. Today. Listen for the weak uh. Festiv-ul. Puh-rade. Buh-loon. Now, tell me. When you were little, what were you scared of?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! The show is in three days. We're practicing every day. Say it with me. We're practicing every day. Great! We use be plus ing for actions happening now, and also for things we're doing these days. Haru is playing the drum, and Riko is singing. 「この ごろ ずっと している こと」も 進行形で いえるよ。 Let's practice. Kiko is dancing. Birimo is clapping. I'm counting. One, two, three, four. We're getting better and better. Mistakes are OK. Let's try it one more time! Now, phonics. Celebration. Invitation. Competition. Information. The ending t i o n says shun. Is our show a competition? No, it's a celebration! Everyone can enjoy it. The audience can clap and dance with us. It will be a happy day. Now, tell me. What are you practicing these days?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Let's decide the program for our show. When we suggest an idea, we can say, Why don't we sing together? Say it with me. Why don't we sing together? Super! It looks like a question, but it means, let's try this idea. Why don't we ～? は「～しない？」と ていあんする いいかた。 Answer, That's a great idea! Or give another idea. How about a dance at the end? Let's practice. Why don't we play the drums first? Why don't we invite the audience to dance? Listen to all the ideas. Every idea is welcome. Say thank you for every idea. Be kind. Now, phonics review. Scratch. Hedge. Station. Action. The spellings are t c h, d g e, and t i o n. Now, tell me your idea for a class party. Why don't we...?

My friend lives by the sea. She plays the drums. Say it with me. My friend lives by the sea. She plays the drums. Great! Don't forget the s! Lives. Plays. He doesn't like spiders, but he loves bananas. Who is it? Birimo! 3人称の s を わすれずに。 Does she like music? Yes, she does. Does he like spiders? No, he doesn't. Does she like cats? Yes, she does. Now, phonics review. Knock. Knee. Wrap. Lamb. Silent letters! The k, the w, and the b are quiet. Now, tell me about a friend. You don't need to say the real name. Where does your friend live? lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, let's compare now and yesterday. In Windy Plains, we learned be plus ing. In the Ruins of Memory, we learned the past. I'm dancing now. Yesterday, I swam. Say it with me. I'm dancing now. Yesterday, I swam. Fantastic! For now, use am, is, or are, and ing. For yesterday, use the past form. いまは ing、きのうは 過去形。 Let's practice. What are you doing now? I'm making a lantern. What did you do yesterday? I played on the beach. Swim becomes swam. Eat becomes ate. Go becomes went. Make becomes made. Now, phonics review. Danced. Clapped. Carried. Played. Drop the e, double the p, change y to i, or just add e d. Now, tell me. What did you do yesterday? What are you doing now?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, let's make a five-sentence speech. Sentence one, Hello. Sentence two, I'm and your name. Sentence three, I like something. Sentence four, Last year. Sentence five, Next year. Listen. Hello. I'm Kiko. I like music. Last year, I couldn't swim, but now I can. Next year, I'm going to learn the drums. Say it with me. Hello. I'm Kiko. I like music. Great! 5つの ぶんで、いまと むかしと みらいを はなそう。 Use the present, the past, and the future. You can use a nickname. Look at Haru's speech. Hello. I'm Haru. I like soccer. Last year, I went to Sunrise Harbor. Next year, I'm going to climb a mountain. Now, phonics review. Future. Near. Again. Celebration. Danced. Now, make your speech. Hold up five fingers and count. One, two, three, four, five!

lessons.teacherScript: Good evening, everyone! Tonight is rehearsal night. Here are three tips for a great show. Speak slowly. Look at the audience. Say it with me. Speak slowly. Look at the audience. Perfect! Tip number three. Take a deep breath and smile. Are you nervous? It's OK to be nervous. Everyone feels nervous before a show, even teachers. きんちょうしても だいじょうぶ。ゆっくり はなそう。 Let's practice. Speak loudly. Don't speak too fast. Look at your friends' faces. Speak slowly, and smile. If you forget a word, that's OK. Take a breath and try again. Your friends will help you. We are a team! Now, phonics review. Learn. Festival. Bridge. Waving. Now, stand up and say your first sentence. Speak slowly. Look at me. Great job! You're ready for tomorrow. I believe in you!

lessons.teacherScript: Good evening, everyone! It's the night before the festival. Tomorrow is the big day! Say it with me. Tomorrow is the big day! Great! How do you feel? I can't wait for the festival! I can't wait means I'm so excited. I can't wait は「まちきれない」と いう いいかた。 Let's check. Are the costumes ready? Yes, they are. Are the lanterns ready? Yes! segments.say: Quiz time! You want a friend to dance with you. What do you say? A, Would you like to dance with us? B, Thank you for coming. Think!
segments.subtitleJa: クイズ！ ともだちを ダンスに さそいたい。なんて いう？ A Would you like to dance with us? B Thank you for coming。かんがえて！
segments.subtitleEn: Quiz time! You want a friend to dance with you. What do you say? A, Would you like to dance with us? B, Thank you for coming. Think!

segments.say: It's A! Would you like to dance with us? And it's always OK to say, Maybe next time. Perfect!
segments.subtitleJa: こたえは A！ Would you like to dance with us? ことわる ときは Maybe next time でも いつでも OK。かんぺき！
segments.subtitleEn: It's A! Would you like to dance with us? And it's always OK to say, Maybe next time. Perfect!

slide.title: Answer
items: Would you like to dance with us?

segments.say: You finished Stage 2! I'm so proud of you. You can host a festival in English! Next, talk with Birimo! ビリモ と おはなし してね.
segments.subtitleJa: ステージ2 クリア！ みんなを ほこりに おもうよ。えいごで おまつりの しかいが できるね！ このあと ビリモと おはなし してね。
segments.subtitleEn: You finished Stage 2! I'm so proud of you. You can host a festival in English! Next, talk with Birimo!

slide.title: Today's wrap-up
items: Thank you for coming to our festival!
Would you like to dance with us?
This is our 600th lesson. We did it!

segments.say: Next is Stage 3. World 21, the Tower of Messages! From now on, English only. You can do it! See you!
segments.subtitleJa: つぎは ステージ3。ワールド21、ことづての塔！ これからは えいごだけ。きみなら できる！ またね！
segments.subtitleEn: Next is Stage 3. World 21, the Tower of Messages! From now on, English only. You can do it! See you!

slide.title: Next
items: Thank you, Ms. Emma! Next, let's go to the Tower of Messages!
